beats.trigger: You built something. It works. Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: The unease I already have about my agent is the normal state, not a sign I'm doing it wrong.

beats.trigger: The story works because classical software is deterministic (same input, same output).
beats.got: Old security assumed the same input gives the same output, and agents don't.

beats.trigger: Your firewall doesn't see it because your firewall has never had to worry about persuasion.
beats.got: A document my agent reads can talk it into acting, and that's the attack, not a break-in.

beats.trigger: Neither lens makes you an expert. The reusable check is the expert.

beats.trigger: *"Hope it doesn't happen"* is not one.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: After modules of giving the agent more, the next move is giving it less, and I sign for what I lose.

beats.trigger: Avoidance beats reduction. Scope beats patch. Don't-open beats mitigate.
beats.got: The cheapest fix is not connecting the thing. That's reasonable, but I've heard it as common sense before.

take_homes: Two reports I got from my own agents: a send-without-review clause in the pricing memo agent, and a source that claims to be redacted but still names people. I want to fix both.
Giving the agent less access is a legitimate fix. After any mitigation I write down the residual and decide to accept it or close the door.
A packaged check (the skill) found things my one-off reading missed, so it is worth keeping and re-running.

monday.when: Monday morning, before the brief goes out

monday.blocker: The skill lives in my project folder only. My team has no shared place for it or for the context files, so they can't run the same check.

misconception.why: The most useful things were the audit findings and a reusable check, not better wording. The send clause and the false redaction header were file and rule problems that no prompt would have fixed. I still think prompts matter some.

one_line: Good hour on my own pricing agents: it found a send clause and a fake redaction I'd missed. The middle repeated itself, and I still can't share the check with my team.
